Write an employer-facing cover letter tailored to this job. Use only candidate facts from the source. Preserve contribution level, shared results, dates, credential status and academic/project context. Do not turn job requirements into candidate history. Choose the strongest relevant evidence, retain useful concrete detail, and write clear natural professional English. Make a focused case through one or two relevant examples rather than reciting the résumé. Avoid generic praise and invented motivation. Use 2–4 paragraphs, at most 320 words, a salutation and signoff.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Junior Data Analyst position at Example C05 Services. My Data Analytics diploma studies at Example Technical College (2026) include Python pandas, SQL joins, Power BI, and data-quality checks. I also bring practical attention to record accuracy from my Retail Assistant role at Example Corner Market, where I checked shelf prices against the till file and reported discrepancies to the shift manager.

In a three-student 2026 course project, I cleaned a public transit dataset in Python and identified duplicate journey identifiers before the team joined route tables. I built the team’s Power BI view comparing median delay by route and weekday. To make the analysis transparent, the report excluded cancelled trips and stated that limitation beside the chart. I then presented the cleaning decisions to the class. This was coursework and the dashboard was not deployed by a transit agency.

This project gave me directly relevant experience documenting data limitations, building a clear Power BI report, and explaining analysis choices to colleagues. I would welcome the opportunity to apply this foundation to operational datasets at Example C05 Services.
